newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela Maracaibo channel may close for 3 hours.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela Maracaibo channel may close for 3 hours.

text.p: Venezuela's principal oil export route could close to tanker traffic for three hours on Thursday due to a protest by local fishermen, the Lake Maracaibo port captain said on Wednesday.
Lake Maracaibo shipping channel, which carries over a million barrels of crude oil daily, would close "partially" from 0900 to 1200 local time (1300 to 1600 GMT), said Captain Regulo Dominguez.
However, shipping agents in Maracaibo said they expected the Coast Guard to keep the channel open despite the protest, and this was confirmed by the Coast Guard.

"They are not going to affect shipping," a Maracaibo Coast Guard official said. "The protest is symbolic and they are not allowed to close the channel and if they try it we will act becuase we cannot allow the canal to be shut."

Port captain Dominguez said tanker traffic would be little affected in any case because high tide is not until 1234 local time (1634 GMT) and fully-laden tankers can pass only at high tide due to draught restrictions in force since last month.

The protest is intended to support a legal claim by fishing union Fetrapesca for a reported $292.5 million against the owners of the Nissos Amorgos tanker which spilled 25,000 barrels in the channel on February 28.
Fransisco Arias, the governor of Zulia state which administers Lake Maracaibo, told Congress on Wednesday he would lead the protest.
